Who operated the fleet. Who runs the 2026 drain. The key-compromise vector.
Consolidation vs theft - ~50/50, a judgement not a measurement.

identity: LastWinner (LW) - the most successful FoMo3D clone, launched 2018-08-06 by a Chinese team, fronted by Android+iPhone apps, promoted by a fundraising-pyramid crowd ('蟎群传播' / Ant Swarm). Source never verified. Straight FoMo3D code fork (getPlayerVaults, getPlayerInfoByAddress, registerNameXID, withdraw() selectors all present; joke fn atInversebrah). 2018 reports allege the operator pre-loaded a large amount of ETH (a soft ~200,000 ETH estimate) for bot transactions to fake activity.
history_2018: ~270k tx in the first 6 days; briefly out-traded the original FoMo3D; then effectively dormant 2019-2025. The contract held 3,970.71 ETH on 2026-03-31.

the_2026_event.one_line: One entity holds private keys to ~44,014 wallets (mostly 2018 LastWinner farmers) and is emptying them: loose EOA ETH first, then each wallet's in-contract game vault via withdraw(), consolidating into a few collector EOAs and mostly PARKING the proceeds.
the_2026_event.public_status: The publicly-reported '2026-04-30 dormant-wallet drain' (WazzCrypto/Specter; Etherscan 'Fake_Phishing2831105' on 0xA707034429...; CryptoSlate/CryptoTimes/KuCoin/Coinpedia et al.) is a DIFFERENT operator (see TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_Apr30_2026_drain). It overlaps THIS ~44k-wallet LastWinner sweep by only ~11-16 wallets. As far as we have found, this LastWinner-fleet sweep has NOT been publicly reported or tied to LastWinner. The public coverage's 'weak/leaked legacy keys' theory for the broader April-2026 wave is relevant context, not a finding about this operation.

TASK1_is_the_unclaimed_2425_ETH_the_same.snapshot: User-provided balances.json: 64,910 addresses with a positive getPlayerInfoByAddress vault (win+gen+aff); vault sum 3,390 ETH == contract balance at ~block 25.70M (~20 Aug 2026). This is a MID-CAMPAIGN (~August) snapshot, not March (its scan_date field is stale). Per-address values are on-chain-exact.
TASK1_is_the_unclaimed_2425_ETH_the_same.answer: MOSTLY NO. (1) The fleet's live vaults with value are essentially done: of ~33,374 confirmed fleet members (track-A sweepers), 14,688 already called withdraw(); only 1,268 have a pending vault, totalling 0.04 ETH of dust. (2) A LARGE PART OF THE REMAINING 2,425 ETH IS PERMANENTLY STUCK: spot-check of the top-900 unclaimed by value (29/30) shows they are 2018 CONTRACTS that self-destructed within seconds of each other on 2018-08-16/17 - no code, no key, so ~427 ETH across that sample can never be withdrawn by anyone. (A nonce-0-at-2025 read of these is an artifact: a self-destructed contract has nonce 0 and no later txs.) The remaining ~193 addrs / ~291 ETH of the top-900 are pre-2021-active EOAs = genuinely abandoned players. So the unclaimed 2,425 ETH = permanently-stranded dead-contract vaults + genuinely abandoned wallets, NOT the operator staging anything. No pID-repointing is happening; the drain calls withdraw() straight from the live 2018 EOAs.
TASK1_is_the_unclaimed_2425_ETH_the_same.stuck_vs_abandoned_vs_operator: Largest single unclaimed vault = 0xf3cb6f36fc55fca478da79a9d7c841463108dfda, 163.42 ETH, pID 1, pure 'aff' (house/first-referrer commission) - this one is a real 2018 EOA still active 2026-09-07, not a dead proxy; not withdrawn. The 'sequential pIDs 89135-89157' cluster = 2018 contracts that self-destructed (dead, vaults stuck). So of the 2,425 ETH: a large slice (>=~430 ETH just in the top-900, more in the tail) is PERMANENTLY STUCK in self-destructed 2018 contracts; the rest is genuinely abandoned player EOAs.
TASK1_is_the_unclaimed_2425_ETH_the_same.repointing_mechanism: In the FoMo3D/PlayerBook design LW forks: the pID<->address link is set on first interaction (determinePID: plyr_[pID].addr = msg.sender). To bind a NEW address to an EXISTING pID you use PlayerBook addMeToGame / addMeToAllGames / registerNameX*, ALL of which require pIDxAddr_[msg.sender] != 0 - i.e. you must already control an address on that pID. NO admin override, NO permissionless 'claim this pID'. => repointing is PERMISSIONED (only the pID owner / holder of their key). It CAN be used defensively (a worried owner with their 2018 key binds a fresh secure address and withdraws from it first) but still needs the old key and is a race. Not observed happening in this operation - the drain just calls withdraw() straight from the compromised 2018 EOAs; dead-proxy vaults have no rescue path for anyone.

TASK_july_entity_vs_aug_sep_entity.question: Given the different timeframes (July loose-ETH wave vs Aug-Sep withdraw() wave), are they the same actor?
TASK_july_entity_vs_aug_sep_entity.verdict: SAME actor, ~90%+ confidence. The timeframes are phases of one operation.
evidence_same: SAME wallets, hit in sequence: 24,220 EOAs were swept for loose ETH by BOTH the July collector (0xa279ffef) AND the Aug-24 collector (0x8d7c20e3); 14,688 EOAs did BOTH a loose-ETH sweep AND a withdraw().
0x8d7c20e3 bridges the phases directly: it is the Aug-24 dust collector AND a gas-drip source for the burst-2 withdraw()s.

EVERY phase's collector/gas infra is seeded from a 2018 LastWinner launch-week wallet in this operation's own key-set: burst-1 collector <- 0x0004c3cac4 (first tx 2018-08-08); burst-1 gas <- 0x4ce9f39d (an HTX hot wallet, 2018-08-06); JULY collector 0xa279ffef <- 0x696e01b6 (2018-08-10, itself a track-A sweeper WITH an LW vault); Aug-24 collector 0x8d7c20e3 <- 0x260d1c47 (2018-08-08, itself a track-A member); burst-2 collector 0x5723168b <- 0x86c6391d (2018-08-07).
Consistent MO across all phases: consolidate then PARK, never a fast cash-out (July 2,907 ETH parked at 0xe4a219fbed since 28 Jul; Aug-24 102 ETH parked at 0x8d7c20e3; burst-2 62 ETH at 0x5723168b).
Same target set throughout (LastWinner 2018 fleet + its bankroll clusters); continuous escalation July -> Aug-24 (both loose-ETH + start of withdraw) -> Aug-Sep (withdraw sweep).
TASK_july_entity_vs_aug_sep_entity.residual_doubt: The proven shared-keys situation (11 wallets also drained by the separate 0xA707 actor) means it is *conceivable* two parties with the same keyset ran different phases. But every phase's infra is funded from wallets that are themselves part of THIS operation's sweep set - a second actor would bootstrap from its own wallets, not from ones being swept here. So: same actor.

TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.public_incident: Flagged by researcher 'Specter' + analyst WazzCrypto on 2026-04-30. Drainer = 0xA707034429c8E4E01df056C0CbCf478F0FBeFAd7 (Etherscan label 'Fake_Phishing2831105'). Active 2026-04-29 23:39 -> 2026-05-07. 326.8 ETH from 577 wallets; consolidated then bridged 324.741 ETH via THORChain Router 0xd37bbe5744d730a1d98d8dc97c42f0ca46ad7146 into BTC + XMR. Peak 244 wallets/hour. 'Mixed age of drained wallets supports an aggregated list drawn from multiple historical leaks.' Etherscan co-founder Jeff Schvey: 'likely some 3rd party service has access to the private keys and got compromised.'
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.is_it_our_operation: NO - it is a SEPARATE operation. 0xA707's 577 senders overlap our set by only 11 (of ~25,328 LW withdrawers) / 1 (of ~33k track-A) / 2 (of 64,910 vault holders). ZERO shared infrastructure. Different laundering: 0xA707 uses THORChain->BTC/XMR; our actor uses LI.FI (0x1231deb6f5) and mostly just parks. Our actor's list is ~40x bigger and LastWinner-specific; 0xA707's is a smaller broad 'leaked-key greatest hits' list.
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.overlap_is_INCIDENTAL_not_a_shared_keyst: 0xA707's inbound sender list = 577 wallets (complete). Intersections with our operation: 11 in our 44,014 drained set; 16 ever called LastWinner; 1 in track-A. 0xA707's OTHER 561 victims are a totally different population - first-tx years spread 2017-2026 (NOT a 2018 cohort), 0/120 sampled funded via the same Huobi/BW hot wallets, many funded straight from Binance/other exchanges. => 0xA707 is a GENERIC dormant-wallet / weak-legacy-key drainer (the publicly-reported April-2026 wave); its LastWinner hits are 2.8% of its list, incidental. If it held the LastWinner-fleet keystore it would have drained thousands, not 11-16. Per the 11 shared: 0xA707 took the balance on 2026-04-30 04:10-05:58 UTC; our burst-1 collector 0x8f55b448 swept the residual dust ~2026-05-03/05; some hit again by burst-2 0x5723168b in Aug/Sep. NO shared infra (0xA707 gas-seeded via a Uniswap swap; cashes out 324.741 ETH -> THORChain -> BTC+XMR within a week; 1-ETH side payments to 0x4feea1ca / 0xbb9bb536). Detail: a707_link_shared_addresses.csv + a707_link_analysis.md.
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.what_that_implies_about_the_cause: The 11-16 shared wallets = fleet wallets that ALSO had independently-weak/leaked keys, so BOTH a general weak-key hunter (0xA707) and the fleet-keystore holder (our operation) could drain them; 0xA707 got there ~3 days earlier. This is NOT evidence our operation's keystore leaked widely - it has the COMPLETE clean fleet, 0xA707 does not. It IS consistent with the fleet's 2018 wallet generator being weak (some subset independently crackable). 0xA707 is an unrelated opportunist. (This does NOT by itself resolve consolidation-vs-theft - see TASK2, now ~50/50.)
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.why_not_trivially_weak_keys: 40/40 sampled LW fleet members had NO outgoing tx in 2020-2025 (2 exceptions). The long-running 'blockchain bandit' / ISE-Ethercombing sweepers have continuously drained trivially-guessable keys (small integers, common brainwallets) since 2016. These survived 8 years untouched => the keys are NOT in that trivially-weak class. They resisted casual sweeping but fell to a dedicated 2025-26 effort => a MODERATELY weak RNG (~tens of bits of real entropy) or a keystore/seed leak that only surfaced/was worth exploiting in 2025-26.
most_likely_specific_scenarios_for_the_L: (A) FARMING-BOT KEY STORE. The 2018 FoMo3D-clone farming operations needed thousands of funded hot wallets; the bot software held those keys in bulk (a keystore file / DB / config, or derived from one master seed). That store leaked / was sold and is now circulating among multiple drainers. Fits: purpose-made wallets, shared bankrolls, dormant since farming stopped, >1 actor now holding them.

(B) WEAK RNG IN THE 2018 TOOLING OR THE LASTWINNER APP. If the bot wallet generator (or the app's client-side key-gen) seeded a PRNG with low entropy (Date.now(), a counter, PID, JS Math.random()), the real keyspace could be ~32-52 bits - too big for 2016-era casual sweeping, brute-forceable with 2025-26 GPU/cloud once someone realised a whole cohort shared the flaw. Canonical precedent: the Profanity vanity-address tool (32-bit seed, fully brute-forced in the 2022 Wintermute/1inch loss). Independently discoverable => explains multiple simultaneous drainers.

(C) SHARED HD SEED / ONE KEYSTORE FILE. One BIP-39 mnemonic (or one bulk keystore) -> the whole fleet. Fits the ~44% coToken-pool subset and the uniform 2026 roster-style drain; but the fleet is NOT proven to be one operation (its funding is via a shared exchange, ~56% are outside the coToken pool).

(D) 3rd-PARTY CUSTODIAL / BACKEND LEAK (the LastWinner app's server, or a shared wallet service). Matches Jeff Schvey's read; matches 'app that lowered the barrier to entry'. Best fit for the WIDER April-2026 wave / the 0xA707 victims that are NOT LastWinner wallets.
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.app_history_research_2026-09-07: See last_winner_map/app_history_findings.md. LastWinner shipped Android+iPhone apps with a BUILT-IN Ethereum wallet. Official guide allowed create OR import (mnemonic/PK) + a wallet PIN, but 2018 Chinese reviews (Jiemian/Zhihu) say the create-new flow did NOT show / back up / export the private key => effectively CUSTODIAL, team-held keys. On-device (weak RNG) vs server-side generation NOT established - needs the binary or the 2018 front-end JS bundles (lastwinner.me is dead; Wayback CDX has snapshots; commands in the findings file). DIRECT PRECEDENT for scenario (B): SECBIT 'Trust Wallet's Fomo3D Summer' (2024) - Trust Wallet's 2018 iOS build seeded its RNG with srand((unsigned)time(NULL)), producing same-second wallet collisions; >2,100 ETH later drained, and many of those wallets had been created specifically to play FoMo3D. A LastWinner app with the same class of bug would produce exactly this cohort.
TASK_relation_to_the_publicly_reported_A.leaning: (A) or (B). Multi-actor simultaneity most specifically fits (B) weak RNG (independently reproducible) or (A) a leaked store traded to several parties. The custodial nature of the app's create-new flow (D) + the SECBIT Trust Wallet precedent strengthen (B): a team-controlled, on-device-generated keyset with a time-seeded RNG. Confirmation needs the 2018 app binary / its front-end JS, or a researcher publishing the cracked-key structure.

TASK2_theft_vs_legitimate_consolidation.verdict: GENUINELY UNRESOLVED, ~50/50. (Earlier drafts of this file swung between 'THEFT strongly-supported' and '~70/30 consolidation'. Both over-stated. The ~70/30 consolidation lean rested largely on a supposed pre-drain 'wind-down' that turned out to be HTX exchange housekeeping - retracted. See notes_on_interpretation.)
for_theft / compromise: Publicly reported as an attack (WazzCrypto/Specter 2026-04-30, 7+ outlets); Etherscan 'Fake_Phishing2831105' label on a related address.
Part of a broader April-2026 wave of dormant-wallet drains attributed to weak/leaked legacy keys.
At least one affected user publicly treated a drained wallet as their own.
ETH moved directly out of EOAs (no contract exploit) => the operator holds the keys, however obtained.
for_consolidation / rightful holder: One entity holds an ORGANISED set of ~44,000 keys and works it as a roster (incl. 8,868 zero-balance withdraw() calls) - looks like managing a known list, not opportunistic scraping.
PARKS rather than dumps: ~2,907 ETH unmoved in 0xe4a219fbed for 40+ days; only ~325 ETH known bridged out (by the SEPARATE 0xA707 actor).
The victim set is overwhelmingly a 2018 LastWinner farming cohort (bot dividends), not innocent retail savings; a ~44% subset used a shared pool (coToken).
The separate 0xA707 drainer, which DID cash out fast to BTC/XMR, shares only ~11-16 keys - i.e. our operation is not just 'another weak-key sweeper'.
TASK2_theft_vs_legitimate_consolidation.what_would_decide_it: The compromise vector (open question #1). A reproducible weak RNG that anyone can exploit => leans theft/opportunism. A single keystore/seed that only the fleet operator(s) ever held => leans consolidation. Also: if the parked ETH (0xe4a219fbed etc.) is bridged to a mixer / fresh exchange deposit => more theft-like; if redeployed or held => more owner-like.
TASK2_theft_vs_legitimate_consolidation.most_probable_vector: Weak / predictable private-key generation in the 2018 farming tooling and/or the LastWinner app (cf. SECBIT 'Trust Wallet's Fomo3D Summer', srand(time(NULL))). Unconfirmed. This is a concentrated pocket within a broader April-2026 dormant-wallet key-compromise wave - the LastWinner tie is this repo's contribution.

relatedness_of_swept_addresses.verdict: The drained set is a related 2018 LastWinner cohort (not an assembled trove of unrelated leaks), though 'ONE operation' is not proven. Evidence: (1) The 'non-LW' subset isn't separate - a 120-sample of the pure-loose-ETH 'non-LW' addresses shows 74/120 called the LastWinner contract in 2018 and 68/120 had LastWinner as their FIRST outbound action; they are 'non-LW' only because they withdrew their 2018 vault back in 2018, so they showed zero balance in the August snapshot. (2) 0/120 of them ever called the original FoMo3D - this is a LastWinner-SPECIFIC operation, not generic 2018-gambling-wallet key exposure. (3) The LW-vault subset and the 'non-LW' subset have the SAME top first-funders: the six Huobi/HTX + BW.com hot wallets (0x1d1e10e8c6, 0xecd8b3877d, 0x4ce9f39d3a, 0xeb6d43fe24, 0x25c6459e5c, 0x73957709), ~two-thirds of both - i.e. both subsets sourced working capital from the same exchange. (4) ~44% of the fleet also routes through the 'coToken' cluster (0x03cb0021 / 0x105631c6 / 0x62a364f7 / 0xae9b8e05) in 2018-19. The behavioural heterogeneity (tx counts 5-50, varying play intensity, mixed gas prices) is consistent with either one farm used at varying intensity OR a farm plus independent farmers plus retail.
relatedness_of_swept_addresses.the_on-chain_relation: The links are: (a) ~44% of the drained wallets used the Nov-2018 'coToken' pool; (b) ~2/3 sourced working capital from the same six Huobi/HTX + BW.com hot wallets (weak - shared exchange, not a private purse); (c) the uniform 2026 drain (proves the 2026 keyholder is one entity). Two creation waves: Aug 2018 (~63%) and Nov 2018 (~22%).
relatedness_of_swept_addresses.did_EVERY_drained_address_touch_LastWinn: NO. Built a set of every address that ever sent a tx to the LastWinner contract (Etherscan block-range scan, converged at 63,456 unique callers through ~mid-Sep 2018) UNION every address holding a LastWinner pID/vault (balances.json, 64,910). Intersected with all 44,014 drained addresses: CONFIRMED touched LastWinner = 35,527 (80.7%); UNKNOWN = 8,487 (19.3%). By category: withdraw()+looseETH 14,216/14,688 (97%); withdraw()-only 10,279/10,640 (97%); looseETH-only 11,032/18,686 (59%). The 8,487 'unknown' are ~all in the looseETH-only group; the caller-list is only through mid-Sep 2018, and a separate FULL-history 500-sample of that group found 60% did call LW (some in Sep-Nov 2018, past the scan window) => true 'never touched LastWinner' is ~15% of the drained set (~6,500 addrs). Column 'touched_lastwinner' added to drained_eoas.csv (yes / unknown). The non-touchers have the SAME Aug/Nov-2018 creation waves, the SAME Huobi/BW funding route, and 45% used the coToken pool - so they belong to the same broad 2018 cohort, not a separate one. Direct LastWinner interaction across the whole drained set is ~85%.

relatedness_of_swept_addresses.attribution_implication: The drainer holds keys to the COMPLETE fleet of one specific 2018 operation - including wallets that never held a residual vault - not a random subset of a keyspace. That fits 'the original operators / whoever got their whole keystore or seed' better than 'a third party who brute-forced weak keys' (scattered subset). The 0xA707 overlap (11 keys, separate actor) still shows SOME wider leakage - consistent with the keystore having been sold/copied.
relatedness_of_swept_addresses.link_from_the_2018_fleet_to_the_2026_dra: The drain's collectors were gas-seeded from reactivated 2018 fleet wallets (e.g. July collector 0xa279ffef <- 0x696e01b6, itself a fleet wallet with an LW vault; Aug-24 collector 0x8d7c20e3 <- 0x260d1c47, a track-A member). That only re-confirms the drainer holds fleet keys. the_2018_cast.2_the_fleet_funding_route: ~2/3 of the ~44k fleet wallets were first funded by an ETH withdrawal from an HTX/Huobi (5 addrs) or BW.com (1 addr) hot wallet in 2018 (the six Huobi/HTX + BW.com hot wallets). Huobi was THE dominant Chinese exchange in 2018, so this establishes 'Chinese-user / Chinese-farmer capital', NOT a single bankroll operation. There is no identified private 'bankroll' entity. Who actually operated the fleet (one farm? several? farmers + retail?) is UNPROVEN.
the_2018_cast.3_coToken_pool: 0x03cb0021 - a small ETH deposit/withdraw POOLING contract, name()='coToken', ~187 ETH, 552 depositors, active ONLY Nov 4-29 2018. Deployer 0xcbeb72c160 funded from OKX; ZERO on-chain link to the LastWinner deployer or contract. A co-investment / pooled-betting vehicle used by a SUBSET (~44%) of the drained fleet. The strongest evidence that at least part of the fleet was coordinated; NOT the game's operator.
the_2018_cast.note: So the 2,425 ETH still in the contract ~= the vaults of ~1,000 addresses that were contracts and self-destructed in Aug 2018 (no code, no key, permanently stuck) + genuinely abandoned wallets. The drain only ever touched LIVE 2018 EOAs.
the_2018_cast.does_the_2018_200k-ETH_bot-funding_claim: PARTIALLY, and weaker after the HTX correction. SUBSTANCE: there was a large 2018 LastWinner farming set of ~44k wallets, funded via Huobi/HTX withdrawals, playing from launch - consistent with the 2018 Chinese reports of manufactured volume. But we have NOT identified a single 'bankroll' entity (the wallets we thought were that are exchange hot wallets), so 'professionally bankrolled by one operation' is now unproven. NUMBER: '200,000 ETH' is a soft 2018 estimate, not verified here. The punchline stands: that 2018 farming set is what is being drained in 2026.
